title: Closed models [notes postérieures à PS ?] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a 'Récapitulation' (summary) of standard formalism for presheaves on a product A×B of small categories. It sits between two pages of IBM JCL listings that are only scrap paper.

1. The diagram. It shows the categories of presheaves (A×B)^, A^ and B^, plus (Ens).
- p_B denotes the projection A×B→A that 'forgets B'; p_A forgets A.
- The pullbacks p_B^*: A^→(A×B)^ and p_A^*: B^→(A×B)^ are the curved arrows.
- The direct images p_{B*}: (A×B)^→A^ and p_{A*}: (A×B)^→B^ are right adjoints. They are pointwise limits along the forgotten factor: (p_{B*}X)(a) = lim_b X(a,b).
- q_{A*} = Γ_A and q_{B*} = Γ_B are the global-section functors to (Ens).
- The commutativity Γ_{A×B} = Γ_A p_{B*} = Γ_B p_{A*} is used below.

2. Yoneda in the product. For a∈A and b∈B, the representable a×b on A×B is p_B^*(a) × p_A^*(b) =: a⊠b, the external product. Hence X(a,b) = Hom(a⊠b, X) = Γ_{A×B} Hom_{A×B}(a⊠b, X), where Hom_{A×B} with an underline is the internal Hom of (A×B)^. Computing Γ_{A×B} as Γ_A∘p_{B*} or as Γ_B∘p_{A*} gives the bracketed alternatives.

3. Currying. Grothendieck writes ^g a := p_B^*(a) ('gauche', left factor) and ^d b := p_A^*(b) ('droite', right factor). Then:
- ^gX(a) := p_{A*} Hom_{A×B}(^g a, X) is the presheaf b ↦ X(a,b) on B.
- ^dX(b) := p_{B*} Hom_{A×B}(^d b, X) is the presheaf a ↦ X(a,b) on A.
So a presheaf on A×B is read as a functor A^op→B^ or B^op→A^.

4. Extension to arbitrary presheaves. A first version, Hom(L⊠M, X) = X(L,M), is crossed out. The kept version defines the extended bifunctor X(L,M) := Hom_{A×B}(L⊠M, X) = Γ_{A×B} Hom(L⊠M, X) for L∈A^, M∈B^. This is the extension of X: A^op×B^op→Ens to presheaves that turns colimits into limits. Correspondingly:
- ^gX(L) = p_{A*} Hom(p_B^*L, X) =: Hom_B(^gL, X) ∈ B^.
- ^dX(M) = p_{B*} Hom(p_A^*M, X) =: X^M = Hom_A(^dM, X) ∈ A^.

5. The final line states the tensor–hom adjunction Hom(X, Y^M) ≃ Hom(X⊗M, Y), with X⊗M = X⊠M. Here X∈A^, Y∈(A×B)^, M∈B^. It follows from p_{B*} being right adjoint to p_B^* and from the cartesian-closed adjunction in (A×B)^.

Purpose: in the 'Closed models' notes (after Pursuing Stacks), this bookkeeping prepares a study of presheaves on product test categories. Likely uses are bisimplicial-type objects, external products, two-variable (Quillen-bifunctor-like) adjunctions for products of modelizers, and Künneth-type statements. The page itself contains only standard category theory.
errors: Subscripts in the last line are loose. With Y^M := p_{B*}Hom(p_A^*M, Y) ∈ A^, the adjunction should read Hom_{A^}(X, Y^M) ≃ Hom_{(A×B)^}(X⊠M, Y) for X∈A^, Y∈(A×B)^, M∈B^. Writing Hom_B on both sides is inconsistent with the preceding line, which puts X^M in A^.

The notation Hom_B(^gL, X) and Hom_A(^dM, X) is shorthand for relative internal Homs, i.e. p_{A*}Hom(p_B^*L, X) and p_{B*}Hom(p_A^*M, X). This is not a mathematical error, but the subscripts name the target category rather than the category over which the Hom is internal.
The line '^gX(a) = p_{A^}…' should read p_{A*}. This is consistent with the next lines.

ideas.what: Presheaf on A×B as an external-product-represented bifunctor X(a,b) = Hom(a⊠b, X), with Γ_{A×B} = Γ_A p_{B*} = Γ_B p_{A*}
ideas.modern_name: Yoneda lemma for product categories; external tensor product of presheaves; Fubini for limits
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exposé I/IV (topos-theoretic formalism of f_*, f^*, internal Hom); used in Pursuing Stacks for A×B

ideas.what: Currying a presheaf on A×B into functors A^op→B^ and B^op→A^, and extending to all presheaves L, M via X(L,M) = Hom(L⊠M, X)
ideas.modern_name: Currying / exponential adjunction in presheaf toposes; Kan extension of bifunctors
ideas.where_published: similar manipulations occur in Pursuing Stacks (products of test categories)

ideas.what: Adjunction Hom(X, Y^M) ≃ Hom(X⊠M, Y) between external product and relative exponential
ideas.modern_name: Two-variable adjunction (external tensor / cotensor), as in Quillen bifunctors
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Hovey (two-variable adjunctions in model categories, 1999)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine recapitulation of the presheaf formalism on a product category: external products, direct images, currying and tensor–hom adjunction. It is useful only as context for the Closed-models notes and contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: '^gX(a) = p_{A^\wedge}' should read '^gX(a) = p_{A*} Hom_{A×B}(^g a, X)'.
The first line reads: X(a,b) = [crossed out: Γ_{A×B} Hom] Hom(p_B^*(a) × p_A^*(b), X), with annotations 'identifié' / 'identifiés' over the two factors.
The diagram's curved arrows are p_B^* (from A^ to (A×B)^) and p_A^* (from B^ to (A×B)^). The straight arrows are p_{B*}: (A×B)^→A^ and p_{A*}: (A×B)^→B^.
The crossed-out text in the second line is a partial 'p_B^*…'; the line then reads 'a⊠b', with subscript A×B under Hom.
